title: Djémila (Cuicul)
description: Djémila which is also known as Cuicul during Roman times is a UNESCO world heritage centre and is one of the best preserved roman cities in Algeria.
guideText: Djémila which is also known as Cuicul during Roman times is a UNESCO world heritage centre and is one of the best preserved roman cities in Algeria. It was founded under the roman emperor Nerva around 97 AD in an area with a lot of mountains. There are lots of Roman temples, a forum, theatres and colorful mosaics in the city. Additionally, its early christian buildings show how much influence the Romans had on the architecture in the city and also how that style was adapted to the local landscape and culture.

title: Maqam Echahid (Martyrs’ Memorial)
description: The Memorial is one of the most visited and recognized landmarks in Algiers.
guideText: The Memorial is one of the most visited and recognized landmarks in Algiers. Unlike some of the other monuments like the Djemila and Kasbah, it is more of a modern monument than an ancient historical site. It was built to honor those who died during the struggle of Algerian independence in 1982, which was twenty years after Algeria gained independence from France. The monument is made up of 3 different concrete structures that come together at the top. They create a shape that resembles palm leaves and the three sections symbolize different periods of Algerian history.

title: Notre Dame d’Afrique
description: Notre Dame D'Afrique is a catholic basilica in Algiers that overlooks the Mediterranean.
guideText: Notre Dame D'Afrique is a catholic basilica in Algiers that overlooks the Mediterranean. It was built starting in 1858 and opened in 1872 during French colonial rule. It became a very important place of worship for the christians who lived in Algeria at the time.The basilica also represents the interactions and coexistence between the christian and muslim communities in Algeria because according to the basilica’s own historical account muslim algerians visited the basilica alongside christian pilgrims. During this long complicated period in Algerian history, French colonialism brought certain political, cultural and also religious changes to the country.

title: Kasbah of Algiers
description: The Kasbah of Algiers is the historic old city, or medina, of Algeria’s capital.
guideText: The Kasbah of Algiers is the historic old city, or medina, of Algeria’s capital. Its history stretches back to ancient Mediterranean settlement, while much of its surviving urban form developed during the Ottoman period. The Kasbah contains narrow winding streets, traditional houses, old mosques, palaces, markets, and remains of its citadel. Built on a steep hillside overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, its architecture reflects a mixture of Maghrebi and Ottoman traditions. The Kasbah also played an important role in the history and culture of Algiers and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992.

title: M’Zab Valley
description: Discover the Desert Cities of M’Zab
guideText: The M’Zab Valley is a historic region in the northern Sahara known for its distinctive fortified settlements and traditional architecture. Established by Ibadi communities beginning in the 11th century, the valley contains five historic towns built around central mosques. Its compact houses, narrow streets, and carefully planned communities were designed for the desert environment. The valley preserves a unique cultural tradition that has endured for centuries and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Timgad (Thamugadi)
guideText: Timgad, known in Roman times as Thamugadi, was founded by Emperor Trajan around AD 100 as a Roman military colony. The city is famous for its remarkably preserved grid plan, demonstrating Roman urban planning. Its ruins include the Arch of Trajan, a theater, temples, baths, a forum, and a library. Located near the Aurès Mountains, Timgad provides an exceptional view of Roman life in North Africa and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Fort of Santa Cruz
guideText: The Fort of Santa Cruz is a historic fortress overlooking Oran and the Mediterranean Sea from Mount Murdjadjo. The Spanish constructed the fort in the 16th century as part of a defensive system protecting Oran. Its elevated position provided strategic views of the city, harbor, and surrounding coastline. The fortress reflects the periods of Spanish influence and conflict that shaped Oran and remains one of the city’s most recognizable historic landmarks.

title: Tassili n’Ajjer
description: Explore Prehistoric Art in the Sahara
guideText: Tassili n’Ajjer is a vast plateau in southeastern Algeria famous for its dramatic sandstone formations and prehistoric rock art. Thousands of paintings and engravings document people, animals, hunting, ceremonies, and environmental changes over thousands of years. The artwork provides evidence of major changes in the Sahara’s environment and human life. Its extraordinary archaeological and natural importance led to its designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
